parts:
Dear Users and administrators,

I'm trying to run my model on a server more powerful than my desktop but it doesn't work. However the model seems to work well on my desktop and my laptop (windows 10) but even then, I get a  DIC infinite. 
My question is how to correct this infinite DIC?  And why the model doesn't work on the server when it works on the Destop and laptop?


##### Model 
formulaRec1 <- inla.surv(times, Status, subject) ~ 0 + a0 + MesureProtec + Age + Sexe + f(Order, model="ar1") + f(spatial, model=CoxSPDE)

ModelRecSPDE1 <- inla(formulaRec1, family="weibullsurv", data=inla.stack.data(Stack), control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(Stack)),
                      control.compute = list(dic=TRUE,mlik=TRUE,graph=TRUE, waic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE),verbose=TRUE,control.inla = list (strategy = "gaussian",h=1e-15))

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: modelling recurrents events taking into account the order of the events
parts:
On Mon, 2019-08-05 at 07:54 -0700, Abdoulaye GUINDO wrote:
>
> Now there remains the question about the DIC infinite of my model
> that is still unresolved. Do you have any idea?

This is usually an overflow issue, mainly because of an weakly indentified model.

Like DIC would require an integral like

\int exp(x) dx

and if the marginal variance of x is large, then exp(x) at the upper limit
might evaluate to infinity, giving an infinite DIC.

you can check the local dic,

> r=inla(y~1,data = data.frame(y=1:10), control.compute = list(dic=TRUE))
> r$dic$local.dic
[1] 6.933122948 5.876833720 5.084616798 4.556472184 4.292399875 4.292399873
[7] 4.556472178 5.084616789 5.876833707 6.933122931


and you can check what goes to Inf and maybe you see in the data what causes this.

--
Håvard Rue
